Explain how noise-canceling headphones work, simply.

Noise‑canceling headphones block unwanted sound with two main tricks:

  1. Passive sound isolation – the ear cups are thick and seal around your ears, so very little outside noise can get in.
  2. Active noise cancellation (ANC) – tiny microphones inside the headphones pick up the outside sound. Inside the driver, the headphone’s computer generates a sound wave that is the exact opposite (180° out of phase) of that ambient noise. When the two waves meet, they cancel each other out, so you hear much less of the background noise.

Think of it as playing a “reverse shadow” of the outside sound to wipe it out. The trick works best on steady, low‑frequency noises like engines or air‑conditioners.
